precepts.text: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep. In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. Looked up in class: offscouring is a rare noun that means physical dirt or refuse cleaned off an object, or a person rejected by society as an outcast. Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Paul says: “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep.

In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves, which is what Jeremiah calls for: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

Waking up is not only knowing who we are. It is searching our own ways, seeing that “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and turning again to the Lord, lifting up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens. The time is short and salvation is nearer than when we first believed, so there is no time left to stay asleep in the condition we are in.

precepts.text: Put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof. To make provision is to make a way for you to fulfil that lust, to leave doors open for that sin. Why be on the phone with your ex? If you are struggling, delete the apps; put controls on your phone so you cannot go on certain things. People say, I made a mistake, I slipped and fell. No: there was planning, you were talking first, you planned what day to meet up; it was already in your mind. It was a decision, not a mistake. If it is that bad, get rid of social media. Do not say, I can handle it, I am good; that is Satan telling you that, and leaving it open keeps fueling that lust.
precepts.point: Sexual discipline applies inside marriage too. When your wife gives birth, you have to wait forty days, sometimes eighty. When your wife is in her seven days you cannot touch her. And guess what: Satan does not come when you are dealing with your woman; he comes when you are not getting any. That is where the fight starts. So those days are the days you get closer to the Lord: I am going to fast more, I am going to occupy myself with the Lord. That is how you train yourself to have sexual discipline. As men we cannot let pleasure control us.

note.label: Sexual Discipline

precepts.why:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” What does it mean to walk in the Spirit? It does not mean moonwalking or walking on the air. Romans explains it: “But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ”, that is, the commandments and your faith, “and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.” To make provision for the flesh is not walking in the Spirit.

To make provision is to make a way for you to fulfil that lust, leaving doors open for the sin. Why are you on the phone with your ex? You are going to end up banging her. If you are struggling, delete Instagram and delete certain things; put controls on your phone so you cannot go on certain things. People say, I made a mistake, I slipped and fell, I don't know what happened. So you were walking and just slipped and fell on the dude? There was planning. You were talking to him first, and you planned what day to meet up. It was already in your mind. It was a decision, not a mistake.

With porn, if it is that bad, get rid of social media. Do not say, I can handle it, I'm good. That is Satan telling you that, and leaving it open keeps fuelling the lust, because every time you go on you see a bunch of different stuff. Some of you say you repented but leave little doors open, and you fall back into that sin. Sit down and talk to yourself: I am dealing with this, so I need to set things up so I do not fall into it.

Because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”. It is a war: you want to stop, you stop for a week or two, and it comes back. The works of the flesh are “Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness”, all sexual sins. That discipline applies in marriage too: forty or eighty days after your wife gives birth, and her seven days. Satan does not come when you are dealing with your woman; he comes when you are not getting any. Those are the days to fast more and occupy yourself with the Lord. As men we cannot let pleasure control us.

precepts.text: Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer. But if any man suffer as a Christian, one that follows Christ and the commandments of God, let him not be ashamed.
precepts.point: That would be many of our sons and daughters who refuse to listen to their parents. If it isn't jail, it's a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. The parents in righteousness are supposed to oversee who their sons and daughters get hooked up with. That's why God gave children parents.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.” The rulers are a terror to those that do evil. Peter shows the difference between the two kinds of suffering: “But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” One of the titles for this class was going to be suffer not as a murderer.

“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.” Suffering as a Christian means suffering as one that follows Christ and the commandments of God, not Christianity. If we get locked up for doing what is right, and some of us will, we suffer that and glorify God.

The young man in the courtroom is suffering as a murderer, literally. He cannot say the Lord is going to repay them for what they are doing to him; the reason he is being judged is that he broke the laws of the Most High. He broke down crying because he is a wankster, not a gangster. Where are the homies and the shoot-em-up videos now? When you get locked up, nobody cares about your black ass once you are in jail. Esau is the devil for a reason; he lets the little negro run around with a gun killing his own people, and then he busts him, and he becomes property of the state, sweat equity for the prison system.

That is where many of our sons and daughters are going when they refuse to listen to their parents: if not jail, a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. That is why God gave children parents. We were not afraid of the power before; we broke the commandments, so the Lord put this beast over us, and when you mess up with him he has no pity. As they say in the islands, those who don’t hear will feel. Suffer, if you must, as a follower of Christ, never as an evildoer.

precepts.text: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: That would be many of our sons and daughters who refuse to listen to their parents. If it isn't jail, it's a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. The parents in righteousness are supposed to oversee who their sons and daughters get hooked up with. That's why God gave children parents.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works”. The powers that be are not a terror to those of us that keep the commandments of God. Even though we are persecuted for it, it is not a terror to us, because we know what it is about. We are in captivity, but we are doing what God said to do, and they are going to have to answer to the Father for their mistreatment of us.

That is because of this promise: “Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” If I am going to get locked up for doing what is right, I will suffer for that.

Being persecuted for righteousness’ sake deals with a whole different kind of mentality. All the words they say to me will not mean anything, because I am suffering for a worthy cause, and I know that after that, mine is the kingdom of heaven. You can go through that trial and say, the Lord is going to receive me because I did what was right.

That is a totally different mentality than going in as a murderer. Suffering as a murderer, you are still going to get jacked up at the end; you are not getting the kingdom. So do that which is good, and if the rulers persecute you for it, the kingdom of heaven is yours.

precepts.text: He that loveth another hath fulfilled the law: adultery, murder, theft, false witness, coveting and any other commandment are briefly comprehended in love thy neighbour as thyself; love worketh no ill to his neighbour and is the fulfilling of the law.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
James 2:8 says “If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well.” What is the royal law? Romans 13 lays it out.

“Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” What law? Love your neighbour as yourself. “For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet”: every one of those is the royal law. “And if there be any other commandment”, any other commandment regarding your neighbour outside of those, “it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

Love your neighbour as yourself is an abbreviation of the six commandments. Of the ten spoken commandments, the first four are how you observe God, and the last six are how you serve your neighbour: honour your father and mother, don’t commit adultery, don’t kill, don’t steal, don’t bear false witness, don’t covet. Those six are briefly comprehended in that one saying. The ten spoken commandments were themselves an abbreviation.

“Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: no ill like being a respecter of persons, seating the man with the gold ring in a good place and telling the poor man to stand over there. “Therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.” Do we keep it? Yes, you simple Christians. That is the royal law James is talking about, and respect of persons is sin against it.

precepts.text: Now it is high time to awake out of sleep, for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Passover is about the destruction of our enemies and our deliverance from their hands; how fitting in a time like this. Deacon Yoshua in Phoenix said it: prophecy should move us to correction, not entertain us.
precepts.point: The ten horns shall hate the whore, make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her with fire: intercontinental ballistic missiles. Trump badmouths NATO over dues and threatens to end it, and now Europe does not want a long war. Before that comes, we must achieve abstinence, discipline, overcoming, and unity.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The ten horns “have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” That is NATO, formed in 1949, with America at the front. But things are changing. France and Italy are negotiating with Iran for oil through the Strait of Hormuz; Canada says it will never take part in the offensive; Germany warns against an endless war; Spain has withdrawn its ambassador from Israel. They agreed to give their power to the beast, and now they are looking out for themselves.

So as Israelites, the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans scattered abroad, not only here in America, when we see things like this we have to understand our salvation is getting closer. “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: nearer than when we first came to the knowledge. Things are escalating rather quickly, and this conflict is something to keep our eyes on.

A lot of us do not recognize what the feast of Passover is really about: the destruction of our enemies and us being saved from their hands. How fitting that the high holy day comes in a time like this. So we have to increase our focus and buckle down; we are in the midst of war, and our minds should not be in other places.

As Deacon Yashua in Phoenix said last Sabbath: prophecy should move us to correction; it is not for our entertainment.

precepts.point: Now it is high time to awake out of sleep, for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Prepare for war mentally; with all this going on in the earth, staying spiritually asleep is madness.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“Now it is high time to awake out of sleep”. We see all these things going on and some of y’all still stay asleep, not even paying attention to what is going on in the earth. Y’all crazy as hell. You need to prepare ye war, and the first place to prepare is the mind: guard your mind from fear.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” God gave you power, love and a sound mind. Some of y’all are scared. Christ told them to sell their garment and buy a sword, and some are still scared to buy one. Christ said do it.

There is a time and place for everything under the sun, and that time is going to come. So prepare mentally. We are a nonviolent people; all we want to do is serve the Lord. But we will protect and defend ourselves.

Waking out of sleep means not letting fear keep you from doing what Christ commanded. “Now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”, and a mind given power, love and soundness by God is ready for what is coming.

precepts.text: Be sober, be vigilant, because your adversary the devil walketh about seeking whom he may devour. The enemy looks for open doors and distracted people; the moment someone leaves the camp the Christian apologists show up to take them back into the world.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
Waking out of sleep means staying awake: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

You have to stay sober and vigilant, because the enemy looks for open doors and distracted people. As soon as one of y’all gets distracted from the mission, they are coming. That is why every time somebody leaves, we see who shows up: the damn Christian apologists.

They take you all the way back into the world and have you speaking all manner of evil, but they are not telling you to prepare yourself mentally for what is to come. They are just trying to destroy what we are doing. They are not trying to save your soul. They say they are already saved; they are not saved from the nuclear missiles that are about to drop.

So the one who is asleep is the one the roaring lion devours. It is high time to wake up, stay sober, stay vigilant and stay on the mission, because the adversary is walking about looking for whoever drifts.

precepts.text: Take heed that no man deceive you, for many shall come in my name saying I am Christ. Guard your mind from deception; there are men online right now claiming to be Jesus.
precepts.point: Now it is high time to awake out of sleep, for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Prepare for war mentally; with all this going on in the earth, staying spiritually asleep is madness.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“Take heed that no man deceive you.” Prepare ye war: you have to prepare yourself mentally, and part of that is not letting any man deceive you. Do not let deception take you.

“For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” He is telling you that many false prophets and many false Christs are going to rise. And it is happening: there are men online right now literally saying that they are Jesus. Freaking Jesus. Freak ass dude.

Christ said more in the same chapter: “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets”. That is going to happen, and those who are spiritually asleep will be the ones deceived.

So awaking out of sleep is guarding your mind from deception. The time is late, our salvation is nearer than when we believed, and the deceivers are already here. Take heed.

precepts.text: Rulers are not a terror to good works; do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same.” Joseph did that which is good, in Potiphar’s house and in the prison, and he had praise of the same: Pharaoh made him governor over all the land of Egypt.

Keep the commandments. A ruler is not a terror to good works, and the favor that lifted Joseph came by doing good under the power he was under.

precepts.text: Be subject unto the higher powers, for there is no power but of God; whosoever resisteth the power resisteth the ordinance of God.
precepts.point: Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter: be subject unto the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God, and you also have the option to affirm; either way, tell the truth.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter from the vows of Numbers 30. “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.”

The court is a higher power ordained of God, so we are subject to it. You also have the option to affirm instead of swearing. Either way, tell the truth.

precepts.text: Let every soul be subject to the higher powers, for there is no power but of the Most High; the powers that be are ordained of him and do his bidding on the earth.
precepts.point: Sisters forced to wear pants at work should keep a skirt or dress in the car or book bag, change in the bathroom on the way out if they can, and ask the Most High for mercy; these are things done in captivity.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“God reigneth over the heathen”. Romans says how: “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.” There is no power but of the Most High; the powers that be are ordained of him and do his bidding on the earth.

That is why whatever the nations do to Israel is of the Most High, and why Israel should fear him and not the nations. He put it on the spirit of the nations to release the slaves, to institute laws, to bring judgment and to give Israel favor. He sits upon the throne of his holiness, and the shields of the earth belong to him.

precepts.text: Be subject to the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God; whoever resists the ordinance resists God, but rulers are a terror only to the evil, not to good works.
precepts.point: They are to take wives and beget sons and daughters, take wives for their sons and husbands for their daughters, that they may be increased and not diminished, and seek the peace of the city where He caused them to be carried away, for in the peace thereof they shall have peace.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
The Most High told the captives to build houses and dwell in them, plant gardens, take wives, and seek the peace of the city where he caused them to be carried away, and pray to the Lord for it, “for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.” Paul gives the same instruction to a people living under another power: “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.”

Babylon was the higher power over the captives, and it was the Lord that caused them to be carried there. “Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.” To fight the captivity was to fight what God ordained.

“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.” So the captives could buy homes, plant gardens, marry, be increased and not diminished, and have peace in the city, so long as they did that which is good: “do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same”.
